changes.title: crissp refused an option whose -- a chat or word processor had made a long dash
changes.problem: A command copied from Teams, Outlook or Word arrives as 'crissp repair —yes' (an em dash); argparse answered 'unrecognized arguments: —yes'.
changes.fix: The crissp command reads a leading em or en dash in an argument as -- before it parses, for its own options and a guard's; a dash inside an argument stays.

changes.title: crissp repair left an existing project's agreement without the sessions section
changes.problem: 0.1.7 added 'Sessions that stay small' to the template's crissp/CLAUDE.md; crissp repair replaced CRISSP.md but never brought the section into a project's own agreement, so only new projects had it.
changes.fix: The section is crissp's own: repair (key sessions) puts the template's text in place, replacing an old one or adding it before 'Working with the product owner' (else at the end); nothing else of the agreement is touched.

changes.title: E4-F1-02: the Activity page shows each session's history and when to start fresh
changes.problem: The sessions report said afterwards that a request started on a long history; while it happened nobody saw it.
changes.fix: activity.py gives each session the history its last request carried (measure.history: input + cache read + cache write) and whether it is past measure.LONG (300k); activity.js shows the size, and past the line a 'long history' mark with /clear and /compact.

changes.title: E4-F1-01: the agreement says how a session stays small
changes.problem: 42% of requests started on more than 300k tokens of history and used 37% of all tokens (F-18); nothing told Claude or the product owner how to keep a session short.
changes.fix: CRISSP.md, the template's crissp/CLAUDE.md and this repository's have a section 'Sessions that stay small': a fresh session per item, /compact mid-item, heavy output (browser checks, screenshots, logs, searches) in subagents or through run/status, narrow questions, agents on separate parts, the lighter model for routine work.

changes.title: F-19: a change's source may be a plain path or a folder
changes.problem: The dashboard read every changes.json source as {file, symbol}: a project with plain paths got no dashboard at all, and a folder was reported as "source not found". The template did not say the format.
changes.fix: collect.py source() reads a plain path as that file from the top; locate() finds a folder and lists its files; the template's changes.json says the format in its "about".

changes.title: F-20: crissp repair puts changes.json's sources and the .mcp.json pin in place
changes.problem: A project that wrote plain paths as changes.json sources, or still pinned an older crissp in .mcp.json, kept them: crissp repair did not look at either.
changes.fix: repair.py fix_changes turns a plain path into {file, symbol: ""}; fix_pin moves the crissp==X pin of the crissp MCP server to the crissp that repairs (CRISSP_VERSION, which the crissp command now passes its engine). Nothing else in either file changes.

changes.title: E3-F3-01: an Activity page, what the orchestrator and its agents do now
changes.problem: The session pages are written afterwards; while Claude worked, the dashboard did not show what the main thread and its subagents were doing.
changes.fix: lib/activity.py reads this repository's transcripts written in the last half hour (with sessionview's own parsing and masking): per session the title, last prompt, the orchestrator's latest step and since when, busy or quiet, and each subagent, running or finished (its own record says so), with its own latest step. /activity serves dashboard/activity.html, which asks /dashboard/activity.json every two seconds; Activity is a section of the one top bar.

changes.title: E3-F2-01: the board shows how the backlog moved
changes.problem: The board was a snapshot: a PBI that went to review an hour ago looked the same as one that had stood there for a week, and nothing said what moved.
changes.fix: lib/movement.py replays the epic files through every commit that changed them with the crissp tool's own parser (three-level ids too, any encoding in history) and adds the working tree's uncommitted state; collect.py gives every PBI its moves and since-when, and the board the newest moves. The board shows 'Moved recently' (from → to, when, commit or not committed) and on each card how long it has stood in its column. The server also watches .git/logs/HEAD, so a commit shows at once.

changes.title: E3-F1-01: one top bar on every page
changes.problem: Each page wrote its own sections: Tests · UX · Workers · Sessions on the Tests dashboard, Tests · UX · Workers on the workers page and the UX suite, Tests · UX · Sessions plus the dashboard's tabs on the session pages; the backlog was only a tab.
changes.fix: look.js holds the one list (Tests, Backlog, UX, Workers, Sessions) and fills every page's empty sections nav, marking the open one (Backlog when the Tests page shows #board). The session and report pages load look.js too, so they no longer carry a second theme switch.

changes.title: E2-F1-01: the dashboard opens whatever encoding an old commit holds
changes.problem: F-16: measure.py's git() decoded `git show` strictly in the locale's encoding, so one old backlog file saved on Windows (cp1252, a middle dot 0xb7) stopped the dashboard with a UnicodeDecodeError; under a Latin-1 locale the pages then failed to be written (◐).
changes.fix: git() reads bytes and decodes UTF-8, else cp1252 (so a Windows file keeps its · and its items their statuses), a byte that fits neither becoming U+FFFD; every read_text and write_text of measure.py, sessionview.py and collect.py names encoding="utf-8", and a test keeps it that way.

changes.title: F-13: parallel workers share one PostgreSQL server, a database each
changes.problem: Nothing in the framework or the template said how tests that need a database run in a parallel step, so a server per worker (memory and start-up per CPU) was the easy way.
changes.fix: CRISSP.md, the template agreement and the testsuite README say: one PostgreSQL server for the run, a database per worker, named after PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER, made and dropped by a session fixture (the README has an example).

sources.symbol: Tests that need a database share one PostgreSQL server
Parallel tests share one PostgreSQL server

changes.title: E1-F1-04: the /workers page
changes.problem: Nothing showed how a run's tests were divided amongst the processors and memory the machine has, nor what each worker was doing.
changes.fix: lib/workers.py state() reads results/timing (start, collected, tests, finish, the workers' now files of this run only) into the machine, what a parallel step would get, and per step its status (running, passed, failed, or stopped when its process is gone), progress, an estimate of what is left, outcomes and one lane per worker (now and since when, quiet after a minute, done, busy). serve.py answers /workers (to dashboard/workers.html) and /dashboard/workers.json; the page asks every two seconds, in the shared look, linked from Tests and UX.

changes.title: E1-F1-03: every test as it finishes, per worker
changes.problem: A run left only its JUnit file at the end: nothing said, while it ran, which worker ran what, since when, or what failed.
changes.fix: lib/pytest_plugin/crissp_timing.py, loaded by covered (-p crissp_timing, its own folder on PYTHONPATH), writes results/timing/<step>.jsonl: start (WORKERS and WORKERS_WHY), collected, every test as it finishes (outcome, seconds, worker), finish. Each xdist worker replaces <step>.now.<worker>.json with the test it runs now. A pytest a test starts itself stays quiet; a write that fails is dropped. run.py names the folder and clears the step's timing at the start.

changes.title: E1-F1-02: a step's tests in parallel processes, coverage still whole
changes.problem: Every step ran its tests one at a time in one process, on one of the machine's CPUs.
changes.fix: A step may say parallel (and memory_mb). run.py gives it WORKERS and WORKERS_WHY from lib/workers.py, prints the count and keeps it in steps.jsonl. With more than one worker, covered runs pytest-xdist with --dist loadfile and measures every worker through an rcfile (parallel, patch = subprocess), then combines. pytest-xdist is pinned. crissp check --plan says each parallel step's workers and why. This project's tools step and the template's backend step are parallel. Coverage is measured one way on one worker or many (the rcfile always), so the gate sees the same numbers on a 2-CPU runner as on a 16-CPU laptop.

changes.title: E1-F1-01: how many workers a step gets on this machine
changes.problem: Nothing in crissp knew the machine it ran on: a run used one CPU, and a fixed worker count would be wrong on every machine but one.
changes.fix: lib/workers.py reads the usable CPUs (process_cpu_count, a cgroup cpu.max) and the memory and what is available (macOS sysctl and vm_stat, Linux /proc/meminfo and a cgroup memory.max). A step's workers are the tightest of: the CPUs less one, three quarters of the available memory per memory_mb, and its test files; at least 1; CRISSP_WORKERS overrides. What cannot be read is unknown, never an error.

changes.title: F-11: a design had no moderator result
changes.problem: In a design run the moderator checked the design and had the designer fix it once, but wrote nothing down. proposal.json held only the designer's part, so neither the results nor the UX suite showed the moderator's word on a design. A round does have it, in round.json.
changes.fix: The proposal prompt names the moderator and has it write check.json (verdict ready / ready-with-remarks / not-ready, summary, found with fixed or not, remaining) before the run may say done. versions() carries it as `check`, and the Designs tab shows it under the design, or says that a finished design has none.

changes.title: F-10: the framework named no place for the product, and nothing put a project back in place
changes.problem: CRISSP.md only said 'the root keeps the product'. The template's steps pointed at src/ with no `when`, its UX suite walked a Vite dev server (127.0.0.1:5173), and deploy.json expected app/backend and app/frontend. So a first session hand-built a prototype inside crissp/uxsuite/ and served it as the product. The template's agreement also named a crissp/tool an installed project does not have.
changes.fix: D-02: app/backend + app/frontend + docker-compose.yml is the default (CRISSP.md 'The product's place', the template's agreement). The template's steps (backend, backend-lint, frontend) exist once their part does, and the UX suite walks the Compose stack (8080). crissp repair (lib/repair.py) shows what a project has out of place: old steps, the old UX address, files in crissp/uxsuite/, the old agreement line, missing template files, an old CRISSP.md, missing ignore rules. crissp repair --yes puts each in place; it never deletes, never commits and never changes the backlog's content.

changes.title: F-09: crissp dashboard opened another project's dashboard
changes.problem: test.sh reused any crissp dashboard answering on the port without checking which project it served: with one project's dashboard running, crissp dashboard in a second project opened the first, so the second's tests and UX results seemed missing. The crissp tool's dashboard action had the same check.
changes.fix: The stamp (/dashboard/stamp) names the project it serves; lib/place.py picks the port: this project's dashboard is reused, another project's (or one that does not say whose) is left alone and the next free port taken with a note, a program that is no dashboard on the asked port stops it with a clear message. The tool's served() also requires the stamp to name its project.

changes.title: F-08: every green full run asked for a commit that only recorded a hash
changes.problem: The gate rewrote coverage-baseline.json on every green run of every suite, with only a new commit hash when no number changed, so every full run ended with 'the coverage baseline went up: commit …'.
changes.fix: lib/gate.py writes the baseline only when something moves: no baseline yet, --accept, a number that changed, or a commit the diff rule needs (none recorded, or one git no longer knows). Otherwise the older commit stays: the next diff rule looks back further, stricter, never laxer.

changes.title: F-01: crissp refused every option meant for a guard
changes.problem: crissp check --plan, crissp deploy --cluster and crissp ux --shoot <walk> were refused: argparse's REMAINDER does not pass a leading --option on to a subcommand.
changes.fix: src/crissp/cli.py splits the command line at the guard's name and passes the rest to the guard untouched.

changes.title: F-02: approving a design failed in an installed project
changes.problem: The UX suite looked for the crissp tool only inside the project; a project made with crissp init has none, so Approve answered 400.
changes.fix: ux_backlog.tool() uses the project's own crissp/tool, else the engine's; designs show before and after with Approve, Approve with a remark, Again and Reject, and a remark comes first in the PBI.

changes.title: F-03: pytest 9.0.3, and a UX test that read the wrong project
changes.problem: The CVE audit flagged pytest 8.4.2 (PYSEC-2026-1845); a UX test inherited the run's CRISSP_ROOT and read this repository during a full run.
changes.fix: pytest 9.0.3 pinned in crissp/testsuite/requirements.txt; the test starts ux.sh without CRISSP_ROOT.

changes.title: F-04: an installed project's guards named script paths it does not have
changes.problem: In a project made with crissp init the guards said 'crissp/deploy.sh may go', 'run crissp/check-all.sh': files that only exist in a repository that carries the framework.
changes.fix: The crissp command sets CRISSP_COMMAND; project.speak() and the Speaking stream every guard writes through name crissp check, check-all, deploy, dashboard and ux instead; deploy.sh's messages and the UX suite's (and the PBIs it writes) do the same.

changes.title: F-06: the first full run did not say what was left
changes.problem: A new project's first green full run ended with 'the coverage baseline went up: commit …', which a new user could not place.
changes.fix: check.py tells a first baseline (not in git yet) from a raised one, and for the first says plainly: commit it, then crissp check moves the certificate, with the exact commands.

changes.title: check.sh crashed outside a git checkout
changes.problem: The repository was taken out of git to become a project of its own; check.sh then failed on git commands with no clear reason, and check-all.sh refused to prove the tree at all.
changes.fix: lib/check.py (check.sh and check-all.sh are its doors) asks first whether the project is a git checkout: check.sh stops with exit 2 and says to run git init and commit; check-all.sh still runs every step for proof and writes no release certificate.

changes.title: The guards named one product's parts in their code
changes.problem: impact.py, run.sh, the gate, the certificate, setup and the audit named a backend, a frontend and their tools in code, so every other product had to edit the framework itself.
changes.fix: One configuration, crissp/testsuite/suites.json (lib/project.py), describes the product's steps (folder, command, coverage, gate), what a change runs (paths), its shared ground, setup and audit; every guard reads it, and run.py runs the steps.

changes.title: The tools found the project from their own file location
changes.problem: Every library reached the repository's root with Path(__file__).parents[n], so the engine could not live apart from a project's data.
changes.fix: The project is CRISSP_ROOT or the current directory (the scripts export CRISSP_ROOT); only the engine's own files (the dashboard page, the look, the UX page) are found next to the code.

changes.title: The Tests dashboard and the UX suite looked different and ran apart
changes.problem: The dashboard and the UX suite had their own looks, ports and servers, and nothing linked an approved design to the PBI it became.
changes.fix: One local server (lib/serve.py) serves /dashboard/, /ux/ and the shared look in crissp/look (tokens, font, theme, water), and nothing else of the repository; an approved design becomes a PBI through the crissp tool, and the board links it back.

changes.title: crissp init and repair onboard Mistral Vibe (F-24)
changes.problem: init registered the crissp MCP server only for Claude Code (.mcp.json); a Vibe session in a new project had to hand-write .vibe/config.toml and edit ~/.vibe/trusted_folders.toml itself, so neither the crissp tools nor the project-local config loaded.
changes.fix: init writes .vibe/config.toml from a new template file (uvx crissp==<version> mcp, the same pin as .mcp.json), merges .vibe/ into the project's .gitignore, and adds the project folder to $VIBE_HOME/trusted_folders.toml when a Vibe home exists (never removing entries, never overwriting the config); with no Vibe home it says so. crissp repair (key vibe) puts the same in place in projects brought in earlier.

changes.title: the Vibe onboarding detects the system and the installation (F-25)
changes.problem: The F-24 onboarding assumed a POSIX machine: it never named the system, never checked whether vibe is on PATH (only whether ~/.vibe exists), and wrote the project path into trusted_folders.toml unescaped — on Windows a backslash path would be invalid TOML and Vibe's own forward-slash entry would be duplicated.
changes.fix: cli.py gains system()/windows()/toml_str() and a vibe_note(): init prints one line with the platform (Windows/macOS/Linux), whether vibe was found (shutil.which plus the VIBE_HOME directory), and what was done; trust paths are written as TOML basic strings (json.dumps) and matched in both backslash and forward-slash spellings; on native Windows init also prints that the bash guards run inside WSL 2 (F-14). repair's trust() does the same escaping and matching.

changes.title: Vibe's trusted folders are read with tomllib, in one place for init and repair (F-26)
changes.problem: trusted_folders.toml was edited line by line in two copied functions (cli.py trust_vibe, repair.py trust): a Windows path was added again on every run (the escaped entry never matched), a one-line `trusted = ["/a"]` became invalid TOML, a folder under `untrusted` was reported as trusted, and repair's fix_vibe still matched the unescaped path, so on Windows it was always out of place.
changes.fix: One engine module, crissp/testsuite/lib/vibe.py (standard library): it reads the file with tomllib, compares paths in both slash spellings, never trusts a folder under `untrusted`, leaves a file it does not know (anything but the two lists of strings) untouched, and writes the file back in Vibe's own shape. repair imports it; cli.py loads the same file from the engine (engine_module). The copies are gone.

changes.title: crissp repair moves the Vibe pin along with the .mcp.json pin (F-27)
changes.problem: repair moved .mcp.json's crissp==<version> to the crissp that repairs, but never .vibe/config.toml's, so after an update Claude Code and Vibe ran different crissp versions.
changes.fix: fix_vibe_pin (repair key vibe-pin) reads .vibe/config.toml with tomllib, finds the crissp server's crissp==<version> argument and replaces only that string in the text, so comments and other servers stay; a config that is not TOML, has no pin, or holds the pin's text more than once is left as it is.

changes.title: crissp init asks before trusting the folder in Vibe (F-28)
changes.problem: init added the folder to Vibe's trusted_folders.toml without asking, also without --yes; trusting is the security decision Vibe's own prompt exists for, and init did not say how to undo it.
changes.fix: vibe_note takes a confirm: without --yes init asks 'Trust <folder> in Vibe (<file>)? [Y/n]' (Enter is yes) when the folder is not listed yet; no leaves the file untouched and says how to trust it later; a trust says how to undo it. --yes trusts as before.

changes.title: .vibe/config.toml is committed like .mcp.json (F-29)
changes.problem: .vibe/ was git-ignored as machine-specific, while .vibe/config.toml holds the same pin as the committed .mcp.json: every teammate had to run crissp repair to get Vibe's crissp tools.
changes.fix: The template's .gitignore rules (and this repository's) are `.vibe/*` and `!.vibe/config.toml`: the config is committed, anything else Vibe keeps in .vibe/ stays local. (A plain `.vibe/` would keep git from re-including the file.) This repository's own .vibe/config.toml is committed.

changes.title: The template lints the frontend as well as the backend (F-30)
changes.problem: The project template had a backend-lint step (ruff) but no frontend lint: a project's frontend was tested, never linted, and a change under app/frontend/ ran no lint.
changes.fix: The template's suites.json has a frontend-lint step, `npm run --silent lint` in app/frontend, which exists once app/frontend/package.json does, and app/frontend/ maps to it. The linter is the frontend's own lint script. crissp repair's default steps come from the template, so they carry it too.

changes.title: A check started with run stayed a zombie, and status could not wait (F-31)
changes.problem: The crissp MCP server started check.sh and check-all.sh but never waited for them: a finished check stayed a zombie, which `kill -0 <pid>` still finds alive, so an agent that waited on the pid run returned hung until its own timeout. status only gave a snapshot, so waiting meant polling.
changes.fix: Every child the server starts is reaped by a thread the moment it ends. status takes wait (and timeout, default 300 s, at most 3600 s): it answers once the lock is free and no check started with run still runs; the dashboard is no run. run's answer and the tool descriptions say to wait with status, not on the pid.

changes.title: The dashboard could stay behind, and findings and decisions were not on it (F-32)
changes.problem: The live server rebuilt the dashboard's data when a watched file was newer than data.js; a change made while collect.py ran was older than the data.js it then wrote, so it was never picked up until the next change. A failed rebuild was only said in the server's log while the page still said live. The board showed epics, features and PBIs only: a new finding or an open decision was nowhere on the dashboard.
changes.fix: Live compares with the newest of what it watches as it was when the rebuild began, so a change during a rebuild triggers the next one. The stamp carries the reason a rebuild failed and the page shows 'not current' with it. collect.py adds the open findings and decisions (through the crissp tool's parser) and the board lists them above the lanes. The dashboard tool says the open page keeps itself current.

changes.title: The workers' command reader is covered on every platform (F-33)
changes.problem: workers._command's last line ran only on macOS (sysctl, vm_stat), so on Linux, where CI runs, lib/workers.py was at 99.5% and the coverage gate was red.
changes.fix: The test of the real sources also runs the current Python as the command: one that prints and one that exits 3, so the output and the None for a failure are both proven on any platform.

changes.title: The frontend is linted with crissp's own pinned tools (F-34)
changes.problem: The template's frontend-lint step ran the frontend's own lint script (npm run --silent lint), but crissp offered no tools or configs for it: a project's frontend lint was missing or assembled by hand, at versions that drift between projects.
changes.fix: crissp/testsuite/frontend-lint/ pins ESLint 9.39.5, @eslint/js, typescript-eslint 8.72.2 with TypeScript 6.0.3, eslint-plugin-react-hooks 7.1.1, eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y 6.10.2, eslint-plugin-react 7.37.5 (only react/no-danger), globals, stylelint 17.16.0 and stylelint-config-standard 40.0.0, with the lockfile and the two configs. lib/frontend_lint.py installs them once per toolkit with npm ci into crissp's cache and runs both on the step's folder with crissp's configs; the project's package.json and files are never touched. The template step runs it (steps.sh's frontend_lint), and the wheel carries the toolkit.

changes.title: crissp lints its own Python with the pinned ruff (F-35)
changes.problem: ruff was pinned in crissp/testsuite/requirements.txt, but no step of crissp's own ran it: the Python in src/, crissp/ and site/ was never linted, locally or in CI.
changes.fix: pyproject.toml has [tool.ruff] (Python 3.12, 120 columns, ruff's default rules plus E402, E731 and N802, which the code's noqa comments already name). suites.json has a `python-lint` step, `py -m ruff check --no-cache src crissp site` with the pinned tools, and every path rule for Python under src/, crissp/ and site/ (and pyproject.toml) brings it. CI runs it with the other quick steps.

changes.title: git lints before every commit: .githooks/pre-commit, turned on by init and repair (F-50)
changes.problem: A project's lint steps only ran in crissp check and CI, after the commit was made; nothing set up a git hook, neither crissp init nor crissp repair, and this repository had none either.
changes.fix: The template's githooks/pre-commit becomes .githooks/pre-commit. It runs `crissp hook` (lib/hook.py: the `lint` and `*-lint` steps that are there, each in its folder with lib/steps.sh and the pinned tools, writing no results) with the crissp .mcp.json pins: the installed one when its version matches, else uvx, else crissp on PATH; in the framework's checkout its engine. crissp init and crissp repair --yes set core.hooksPath .githooks, but never over a core.hooksPath of the project's own or hooks in .git/hooks: those are said. This repository commits the same hook.

changes.title: This repository lints its own bash and JavaScript (F-38)
changes.problem: crissp's own plain JavaScript (the shared look, the Tests dashboard, the UX suite's page) and its bash scripts (the guards, run.sh, setup.sh, steps.sh, deploy/check.sh, site/build.sh) were never linted, locally or in CI.
changes.fix: A `lint` step (crissp/testsuite/lint/lint.sh): shellcheck (shellcheck-py, pinned in lint/requirements.txt, run with uv) on every tracked bash script, ESLint (pinned in lint/package.json and package-lock.json, npm ci when stale) on every tracked JavaScript file, with eslint.config.js declaring the shared window.Look. The paths map runs it for a change to a JavaScript or bash file, CI sets up Node.js and runs it, the audit covers the lint tools. Dev-only: nothing of it is in the wheel.

changes.title: ux.js proposals() no longer reads a key it never uses (F-39)
changes.problem: proposals() read the ?key= of the design to open into a variable it never used (the scroll to that design is in render()).
changes.fix: The dead variable is removed; ESLint's no-unused-vars in the lint step keeps it from coming back.

changes.title: trivy ran as whatever version a machine had on its PATH (F-42, E6-F1-01)
changes.problem: lib/audit.py called trivy from the PATH: an old trivy, a missing one, or a replaced release (as happened to trivy's own releases in 2026) decided what was green, and two machines could disagree.
changes.fix: lib/tools.py pins one version of each scanner crissp brings (trivy 0.76.2, gitleaks 8.30.1) with the SHA-256 of its release archive for Linux and macOS (x86_64, arm64), fetches it once into the crissp cache (CRISSP_CACHE, XDG_CACHE_HOME or ~/.cache), refuses and keeps nothing when the checksum differs, and takes only the binary's bytes from the archive. audit.py runs that trivy; a trivy that cannot be had is a problem, and the other scanners still run.

changes.title: A project brought in with crissp init had no audit, and crissp's own audit skipped its chart (F-42, E6-F1-02)
changes.problem: The template's suites.json had no audit step and no audit section, so a project's dependencies, images, Dockerfiles, chart and Terraform were never scanned. crissp's own audit ran pip-audit only. And an audit that named a place the project did not have yet could only fail on it.
changes.fix: The template gets a full-run audit step (`audit run`, a new steps.sh helper that runs the engine's lib/audit.py) once app/ exists, and an audit section naming the default places (D-02): the backend's requirements, the frontend's lock, both folders for trivy fs, the Dockerfiles, the chart, Terraform, the compose file and the chart's images. `missing: skip` lists a place that is not there yet instead of failing; with none there the audit is green and says so. crissp's suites.json adds trivy config on crissp/deploy/helm/app and crissp/deploy/terraform.

changes.title: Nothing scanned git for secrets (F-43, E6-F2-01)
changes.problem: 'Never in git: keys, .env' was guarded by .gitignore only. A key committed anyway, in crissp or in a project, was found by nothing, and stayed in the history.
changes.fix: lib/audit.py secrets runs the pinned gitleaks 8.30.1 (lib/tools.py) over the whole git history (over the files without git), redacted, into results/secrets.json. Findings carry file, line, commit, rule and fingerprint; the Secret and Match fields are never read. The project's own .gitleaks.toml, .gitleaksignore and gitleaks:allow count. A step in crissp (every part's change runs it, CI scans the full history) and in the template (audit secrets, every change under app/). crissp's one finding, a made-up value in a test, is allowed in .gitleaks.toml by its file and value, with why (F-51: a .gitleaksignore fingerprint names a commit and missed in a shallow clone).

changes.title: No static security analysis (F-44, E6-F3-01)
changes.problem: eval, a shell built from a value, yaml.load, pickle, verify=False, SQL built from strings, innerHTML or child_process.exec in a project's code, or in crissp's own, passed every step.
changes.fix: lib/audit.py sast runs Semgrep 1.185.0 (pinned, through uv) offline with crissp's own 13 rules (crissp/testsuite/sast: Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, JSX) plus the project's rules folders (audit.sast_rules), on the code audit.sast names; ERROR blocks, WARNING is listed, a finding never repeats the code. Every rule has tests (sast/tests, ruleid and ok lines), run by audit rules and by crissp's own sast step before it scans src, crissp and site. The template gets a sast step (audit sast on app) and its backend lint becomes ruff_check: ruff's Bandit rules (S) on top of the part's own ruff configuration, with asserts, made-up passwords and random allowed in tests. crissp's own .semgrepignore keeps Semgrep's defaults from skipping crissp/testsuite (the engine).

changes.title: crissp never asked about several backends or frontends, nor advised splitting a part whose tests take long
changes.problem: The template knew one app/backend and one app/frontend: a big product became one part, every change in it ran all of its tests, and nothing said so (F-60).
changes.fix: CRISSP.md gets Several parts (app/backend-<name>, app/frontend-<name>, each with its own steps; split past about three minutes); the template's first CRISSP block asks the product owner how many parts there are; crissp init says so; crissp/check.sh --plan advises a split for a step over three minutes (the last measured time, else suites.json's).

changes.title: The UX suite's personas could only be edited by hand in team.json, and no rule could be added
changes.problem: The team was an array in team.json with no way to change it in the page, personas had no jobs and could not be switched off, and the rules were one prose PRINCIPLES.md: nothing to add, weigh or switch off, and advice never said which rule it was about (F-61).
changes.fix: ux_cards: one Markdown file per persona (personas/) and per rule (rules/), checked with clear errors; the page's Team and Rules tabs write them through POST /ux/api/persona and /ux/api/rule (same origin only); the first write moves team.json's personas and PRINCIPLES.md's sections into files; rounds and shoots use only the personas that are on, with their jobs; each run gets inputs/rules.md with the rules that hold, and advice names its rule; repair keeps both folders.

changes.title: Ten changes stayed 'missing' on the dashboard although their tests passed (F-40)
changes.problem: The dashboard proves a change by finding its tests in a step's JUnit file. The package step ran pytest without --junitxml, so the tests in package_tests (test_cli, test_package) never reached the dashboard and every change they prove showed as 'missing'.
changes.fix: The package step writes its JUnit to $JUNIT like every other test step. test_changes checks that every test a change names is run by a step that writes JUnit.

changes.title: Lint was only a passed or failed line, and the Suites table called it 0 tests (F-41)
changes.problem: The dashboard had no place for lint: a lint step (backend-lint, frontend-lint) showed only as passed or failed among the steps, its problems only in its log, and the Suites table listed it as a suite of 0 tests, 0 failed, even when it failed.
changes.fix: collect.py treats a step whose key is lint or ends in -lint as a lint step: it gives the dashboard each one with its state and the number of problems its log reports (ruff, Biome, ESLint, Stylelint, shellcheck), and leaves it out of the suites. The Overview shows a Lint tile: clean, or the problems per part, red when one failed.

changes.title: The Overview gave no verdict and its tiles were hard to read (F-70)
changes.problem: To know whether a run may go out one had to read every step. Tiles were named by long uppercase step labels with the tool in brackets, 'Changes proven' said 'every change has passing tests' at 41 of 49, 'Changes by area' was one card holding 49 titles, and every step's log was open on Runs & logs.
changes.fix: The Overview opens with a verdict: ready to release, or not ready with each failed step linked to its own log. Tiles use short names (no 'CRISSP: ', no tool in brackets), line and branch coverage share one tile, a tile says what is not right yet and links to it, steps and suites sit side by side, and per area only the changes not proven yet are listed. On Runs & logs a failed step's log is open and a passed one folded.

changes.title: One long failure made the Tests table 150,000 px wide, and failures were buried (F-71)
changes.problem: A failing test's assertion without spaces to break at made the table grow sideways to 150,000 px; the failures were listed among all the passing tests.
changes.fix: A test's description takes at most two lines, a failure's log wraps anywhere, and failed tests come first.

changes.title: Pages scrolled sideways on a phone, and the primary button's text was hard to read (F-72)
changes.problem: On a 390 px phone the top bar's six sections made it 31 px wider than the screen, so every page scrolled sideways. The primary button was white on the dark theme's light purple, a contrast of 3.2:1.
changes.fix: Below 800 px the sections get a row of their own that scrolls sideways itself. Text on the accent uses --on-accent: dark in the dark theme (6.2:1), white in the light one (5.9:1).

changes.title: The scans showed as suites of 0 tests, and nowhere said what they found (F-73)
changes.problem: The audit, secrets and sast steps run no tests; the Suites table listed each as 0 tests, 0 failed, even when gitleaks had found a leaked secret.
changes.fix: collect.py gives the dashboard each scan with its state and how many findings block the release (its BLOCKING lines), and leaves the scans out of the suites. The Overview shows a Security tile next to Lint; the suites table lists only suites that ran tests.

changes.title: The UX page hid the debate and could not enlarge a design
changes.problem: A round showed only the moderator's summary and advice; the personas' own first looks and their answers to each other were written nowhere the page read. A design was a small frame beside a small screenshot, with no way to see it big or next to today's screen (F-80).
changes.fix: ux_team.versions() carries each round's debate.json, and the round prompt has the team rewrite it as each look and answer comes in, each answer with its debate round. The page shows the first looks as cards (score, good, problems with severity and a link to the shot, ideas) and the answers per round (agrees, disagrees with whom, changed their mind), live while the round runs. Every screenshot and design opens in a viewer over the whole window: before, side by side or after, at fit, 100%, 150% or 200% (keys 1-3, + - 0, Esc), the design still in its sandbox.

gaps: No browser test of the framework's own pages: the dashboard's and the UX suite's JavaScript (app.js, ux.js, look.js) run only in a person's browser; the tests prove the data and the server behind them.
The UX team's rounds and designs are headless Claude Code runs and its screenshots need Playwright's Chromium: both are stood in by the tests, no real round has been proven by a test.
The deploy step needs helm (and terraform for its fmt and validate) on the machine; without terraform that part is skipped with a visible line, not proven.
The CVE audit needs the network (uv resolves the pinned tools, pip-audit asks the advisories): offline the audit step is red, never green.
Without git there is no release certificate: check.sh stops and check-all.sh proves the tree but certifies nothing until the repository has commits.
The coverage baseline starts empty: the first green full run with a commit sets it, and until then the rule that every changed line is covered is skipped.

The dashboard's page is tested by rendering app.js in node with a stand-in for the browser (test_dashboard_page): what it shows, not how it looks. Layout and colours are checked in a browser by hand, with screenshots.
